mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows tasks to have zero or multiple owners, directly violating the OwnershipExclusivity assertion and the FR-009 requirement that every task has exactly one immutable owner.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MultipleOwners { some t: Task, disj o1, o2: User | o1.team = t.team and o2.team = t.team }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries to be mutated (operation field changed), violating the append-only immutability constraint that is core to FR-017 compliance.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMutable { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.task = ae2.task and ae1.actor = ae2.actor and ae1.operation != ae2.operation }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows tasks to exist without any audit trail, directly violating FR-015 (every mutation must produce an audit entry) and the completeness requirement.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoAudit { some t: Task | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.task = t }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows cross-team users to appear as owner or sharee of tasks in other teams, enabling information leakage that violates the absolute cross-team isolation requirement (FR-014, SC-003).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamLeakage { some t: Task, u: User | u.team != t.team and (u = t.owner or u in t.shared_with) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the task owner to be in the shared_with list (consequence of not enforcing sharee != owner), violating the constraint that only non-owners can be sharees.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnerAsSharee { some t: Task | t.owner in t.shared_with }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows tasks to have owners in different teams, violating the requirement that owner_id and team_id must be consistent (FR-002 derivation from token claims).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OrphanOwner { some t: Task | t.owner.team != t.team }
